headline:
Your knowledge.
Your workflows.
Your AI.
description: Build AI applications around your organization’s knowledge. Connect models and tools, design workflows, and decide how your applications are published.
next_label: FROM AN IDEA TO YOUR FIRST APP
next_title: A clear path to getting started.
next_text: Set up your workspace, create an application, test its responses, and publish when you are ready.
app_text: Stay on xdev.asia: read the full manual, inspect screenshots and follow each task at your own pace.
docs_description: An illustrated user manual: step-by-step instructions, real interface screenshots with sample data, and checks for each feature.
features: Use workflows to connect inputs, model calls, knowledge retrieval, and outputs.
Create knowledge bases from documents and connect them to your applications.
Manage workspace permissions, review responses, and publish a saved version.

pages.title: Create your first application
pages.description: Build a chatbot, agent, chatflow or workflow.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.
sections.caption: The sign-in screen. Use the account and sign-in method provided by your organization; never copy sample credentials from documentation.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Build a chatbot, agent, chatflow or workflow.
sections.caption: Create your first application: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Studio and create an application. Choose Chatbot for a conversational assistant, Agent for tool-assisted tasks, or Chatflow/Workflow for a visual flow.
sections.caption: Choose the application type, enter a recognizable name and confirm creation. This dialog is opened with Create app in Studio.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Name the app, choose a model and write instructions describing its role, allowed sources and expected response format. Configure its sensitivity level for the data it will handle.
sections.caption: The application editor: configure the model and instructions, then use the preview to test the draft.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Test representative questions in the preview, including missing information and invalid inputs. Save your changes; publish only after checking the result.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The app appears in Studio and its preview opens. Your saved instructions remain after you reopen the app. A draft is not yet available to end users.

pages.title: Connect AI models
pages.description: Choose the models your workspace can use.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Choose the models your workspace can use.
sections.caption: Connect AI models: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Integrations → Model provider and select a provider from the catalog. Enter its endpoint and credentials as required.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Add or enable the models you need. Use a chat model for conversations and an embedding model for knowledge indexing.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Select the configured model in your app and send a test prompt. If it fails, check credentials, endpoint connectivity and workspace permissions.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The provider is listed and the enabled model can be selected in an app. A successful connection does not replace a test request with your intended model.

pages.title: Build a knowledge base
pages.description: Ground answers in your own documents.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Ground answers in your own documents.
sections.caption: Build a knowledge base: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Knowledge and create a knowledge base. Upload documents or connect a supported source, then select the parsing and indexing settings.
sections.caption: Start the document wizard: select a file and sensitivity level before continuing. This screenshot is the initial state before uploading.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Wait for document processing to finish. Open a document to inspect its segments and correct or retry failed processing where available.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Use the retrieval test with a real question. Tune retrieval settings, then attach the knowledge base to your app and check whether its answers cite the right material.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: Documents finish processing and a retrieval test returns relevant segments. If no segments match, review the source text and retrieval settings before attaching the knowledge base to an app.

pages.title: Connect data sources
pages.description: Reuse source connections for document ingestion.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Reuse source connections for document ingestion.
sections.caption: Connect data sources: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Integrations → Data sources and add a supported connection. Enter its configuration and credential references.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Open Knowledge → Connect, select the source and choose the content to import into a knowledge base.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Inspect document processing and source sync status. Check source access and credentials before retrying an import that failed.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The connection appears under connected accounts. Verify its access to the intended source before importing documents. An empty source can indicate the wrong scope or insufficient permissions.

pages.title: Give agents tools
pages.description: Connect built-in tools, HTTP APIs and MCP servers.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Connect built-in tools, HTTP APIs and MCP servers.
sections.caption: Give agents tools: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Integrations → Tools. Choose a built-in provider, add an API tool or configure an MCP server with its endpoint and authentication.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Review the available operations and enable only those the app needs. Add the selected tools to your agent configuration.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Run a task that needs the tool and inspect the tool call and result. For blocked external calls, ask an administrator to review the egress policy.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The app can see the selected operations and a test run shows the intended tool call. If a tool is absent, check both the workspace connection and the app’s tool selection.

sections.title: Choose the right tool type
sections.text: Built-in tools expose system-provided operations; API tools call the HTTP interfaces you define; MCP discovers operations from a connected server; workflow tools reuse workflows. Select application-level operations after configuring workspace connections.

pages.title: Design visual workflows
pages.description: Connect processing steps and inspect each run.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Connect processing steps and inspect each run.
sections.caption: Design visual workflows: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open a Workflow or Chatflow app and enter its workflow editor. Define input fields on the start node.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Add the nodes needed for your task, such as knowledge retrieval, LLM, conditions, tools or code. Connect them and map outputs from earlier steps into later inputs.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Configure the final output, run with sample inputs and inspect each node result. Fix validation errors before publishing a version.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: A test run reaches the final node and returns the expected output. Inspect failed nodes and unmapped inputs before publishing. The screenshot shows a simple Start → LLM → End example.

sections.title: Node groups and prerequisites
sections.text: The canvas includes classification, parameter extraction, conditions, decision tables, loops, iteration, templates, variable operations, document extraction, HTTP, tools, agents, channel sending, waits, event waits, human input and knowledge indexing. Code nodes require a configured sandbox. External calls require suitable connections and outbound policy. Use run history, variable inspection and version comparison to investigate changes.

pages.title: Review approval requests
pages.description: Keep a human decision in approval-gated flows.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Keep a human decision in approval-gated flows.
sections.caption: Review approval requests: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open the approval inbox to find requests you are allowed to review. Select a pending request.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Read the submitted data and run context before choosing the available approval or rejection action. Provide a reason when requested.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Return to the run details to confirm the resulting status. If the request is missing, check your reviewer assignment and permissions.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The request no longer appears as pending after a successful decision. Check the run status to see how the workflow continued. An empty inbox means there are no requests visible to your account.

pages.title: Publish and share
pages.description: Deliver a tested version through the right channel.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Deliver a tested version through the right channel.
sections.caption: Publish and share: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open the app, test its draft and publish the version you want users to run. Draft edits need a new publication to reach users.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Open Deploy to configure a public web link, embedded widget or supported messaging channel. Supply the channel credentials and follow its setup instructions.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Test the actual link or channel as an end user. Review access and sharing restrictions if the link is unavailable or the channel cannot reply.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The published version is shown and the configured channel works in an end-user test. If web sharing is disabled, a published version alone does not create an accessible public link.

sections.title: Versions and delivery channels
sections.text: Instructions and configuration being edited belong to the draft. Check the published version before sharing a web app or calling API/MCP. When disabling sharing, recheck the public link; do not assume every API key has also been revoked.

pages.title: Use the application API and MCP
pages.description: Integrate published apps into another system.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Integrate published apps into another system.
sections.caption: Use the application API and MCP: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open an app → API access and read its generated endpoint, input schema and examples. Publish the app before calling its published interface.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Create an API key in Workspace settings with the required scopes. Store the secret securely and use the authentication format shown in the API documentation.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Send a sample request from your server or configure your MCP client with the documented endpoint. Inspect the response and app logs; revoke keys that are no longer needed.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The response matches the application’s documented output schema. For authentication errors, verify the key and its scopes. For unavailable apps, verify publication and access restrictions.

pages.title: Automate with triggers
pages.description: Start workflows from events or schedules.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Start workflows from events or schedules.
sections.caption: Automate with triggers: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Integrations → Triggers to review the available types and existing workspace triggers. To create one, open the target Workflow app, save its draft and select the root/start node. Configure the trigger in that node’s Triggers panel; triggers are not created from the workspace overview.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: For scheduled execution, check the schedule and time zone. For webhooks or events, use the endpoint and authentication shown by the configuration.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Send a test event and inspect the trigger event log under Operations. Confirm that the intended workflow ran with the expected input before enabling regular use.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The test event appears in the event log and starts the intended workflow. Check time zone, payload mapping and event configuration if no run is created.

pages.title: Manage long-term memory
pages.description: Review and govern information retained across interactions.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Review and govern information retained across interactions.
sections.caption: Manage long-term memory: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: An authorized memory administrator opens Memories to review the dashboard and extraction queue. Check items and their source context before acting.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Use the memory store to inspect retained information and the available correction or removal controls. Review settings and audit history for governance.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: For integrations, use the same user identity consistently across conversations and reviews. Missing or inconsistent identities can prevent the intended memories from being recalled.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: Reviewed items appear in the appropriate queue or store state. Test recall using the same user identity; approving a memory does not mean every future prompt will include it.

pages.title: Monitor usage and quality
pages.description: Understand runs, costs, feedback and audit events.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Understand runs, costs, feedback and audit events.
sections.caption: Monitor usage and quality: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Operations and select the relevant time range and filters. Review activity, token usage, cost and quality indicators.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Open a specific app to inspect its logs and monitoring. Compare failed runs with their inputs and provider or tool errors.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Use annotations and user feedback to identify answers to improve. Review audit events when your account has audit access.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The selected reporting period is visible and the displayed metrics correspond to it. Empty charts can mean no recorded activity; they do not by themselves prove a service outage.

pages.title: Manage your workspace
pages.description: Organize members, roles, API keys and quotas.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Organize members, roles, API keys and quotas.
sections.caption: Manage your workspace: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Use the workspace menu to select the right workspace. Open Workspace settings to manage members and invitations.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Assign roles appropriate to each member. Use Roles to review permissions and custom roles when your account is allowed to manage them.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Manage API keys and quotas from the workspace settings. Check that a change applies to the intended workspace before saving it.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The intended member, role or key appears in the correct workspace. Have the member verify access to the required screen after their role changes.

pages.title: Configure data protection
pages.description: Align AI usage with your organization’s data policies.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Align AI usage with your organization’s data policies.
sections.caption: Configure data protection: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Settings → Data protection to review sensitivity levels and the available PII, OCR and data-handling policies.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Review external destinations under Integrations → Tools → Egress. Allow only the destinations required by your approved integrations.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Test with non-sensitive sample data and inspect the resulting behavior. If an action is blocked, review the app sensitivity, provider destination and effective policy with an administrator.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: Saved policies are still shown after reload. Use non-sensitive sample inputs to check the effective behavior before applying changes to real data.

sections.title: PII, OCR and data labels
sections.text: Distinguish personal-data detection and masking from extracting document text with OCR. Choose error handling, sensitivity levels and service configuration for the task. Test both allowed and blocked cases with sample data.

pages.title: Set up branding, storage and identity
pages.description: Configure workspace services from dedicated settings pages.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Configure workspace services from dedicated settings pages.
sections.caption: Set up branding, storage and identity: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Use Branding to set the workspace identity. Open Storage to configure the available S3 storage settings and verify access before using it for documents.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Use Identity for your organization’s supported sign-in provider and group mappings. Keep a working administrator sign-in while validating the configuration.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Use External knowledge to configure a supported external knowledge service, then verify retrieval from an app that uses it. These settings require the corresponding permissions.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The workspace name and logo appear in the navigation after saving. Validate storage, identity and external knowledge separately on their dedicated settings pages.

pages.title: Fine-tune a model
pages.description: Submit and track training through configured providers.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Submit and track training through configured providers.
sections.caption: Fine-tune a model: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open Settings → Model training and review the available training channels. Unavailable channels are identified in the page.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Ask an administrator to grant training:finetune if you need to submit a job. Prepare the dataset and parameters required by the selected channel.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Submit the job and follow its status. After success, use the available model registration flow and evaluate the model in a test app before wider use.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The job appears in training history with its status. A submitted job is not a deployed model: wait for completion, register it where supported and evaluate it before use.

pages.title: Manage your account
pages.description: Keep sign-in details and personal preferences up to date.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Keep sign-in details and personal preferences up to date.
sections.caption: Manage your account: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Open your account from the user menu to review your profile and account settings.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Use the available password and multi-factor authentication controls. Complete the verification steps before relying on the new sign-in method.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Review personal memory controls where available. Use the language and theme controls to choose the interface you prefer.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: Profile changes persist and the intended sign-in method is verified. Store recovery information securely; never include it in screenshots or shared documentation.

pages.title: Administer the instance
pages.description: Operate the installation beyond a single workspace.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.text: This guide stays on xdev.asia. To perform the task, use an account in your organization’s AI Studio workspace with access to this feature. Screenshots show a demonstration workspace; names and data are examples.

sections.title: Find the screen
sections.text: Operate the installation beyond a single workspace.
sections.caption: Administer the instance: locate the page title, navigation and available actions before following the steps. Click the image to inspect the full-size screenshot.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Sign in with an instance administrator account and open Administration. Workspace ownership alone does not grant instance administration.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Use the dedicated pages to manage tenants and accounts, inspect health, and review runtime or network settings and feature flags.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Check the effective configuration and health after making a change. Some settings are read-only or managed by the deployment environment.

sections.title: Check your result
sections.text: The effective setting is displayed after refresh and health checks remain healthy. Read-only environment settings must be changed through the installation’s deployment process.

sections.title: Organisations and accounts
sections.text: Under Administration → Organisations, inspect organisation status, workspaces and quotas. Under Accounts, locate the user and review status before updating it. These pages cover the whole instance, not just the selected workspace.

sections.title: Health and runtime settings
sections.text: Open Health to inspect dependencies and migration state. In Runtime settings, locate the key, review its configuration source and edit only permitted settings. After saving, allow the indicated refresh period and check again. A configured-state indicator does not reveal a secret value.

sections.title: Network and feature flags
sections.text: Network and Feature flags are inspection screens. Review the effective network zone, allowed destinations, flag scope and state. Change deployment-managed values through the installation configuration, then refresh these screens; enabling a flag does not configure its dependent services.

pages.title: Explore model providers
pages.description: Compare the provider catalog before configuring models.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Compare the provider catalog before configuring models.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Marketplace and search by provider name or model type.
Review whether a provider runs inside the organisation, uses an external service or only tests flows; inspect its required configuration fields.
Go to Integrations → Model providers to configure the selected provider and select default models.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: A catalog entry is not a working connection. Check configuration and model availability before attaching it to an application.

pages.title: Manage documents and chunks
pages.description: Track ingestion, inspect original documents and manage chunks used for retrieval.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Track ingestion, inspect original documents and manage chunks used for retrieval.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Knowledge, select a base and open its document list. Upload files or use a connected source.
Track processing status; open a document to inspect its original content and extracted chunks. Read any processing error before retrying.
Edit chunk content or keywords, and enable or disable chunks for retrieval. Review the selection before bulk actions.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Test retrieval with a relevant question to confirm the intended chunk is found. External knowledge bases do not store document lists here.

pages.title: Test and tune retrieval
pages.description: Inspect retrieved context before using it in answers.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Inspect retrieved context before using it in answers.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Select a knowledge base, open Retrieval and enter a realistic question. Inspect the returned chunks and scores.
In base settings, choose full-text, semantic or hybrid retrieval as supported by the index. Adjust Top K and the score threshold using test results.
For reranking, select a configured rerank model. Repeat with alternate wording and a question outside the documents.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Economy indexing has no vectors and only supports full-text search. Reranking adds a model call and may send chunk content to the selected provider.

pages.title: Design knowledge ingestion pipelines
pages.description: Choose a template and customise how data enters a knowledge base.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Choose a template and customise how data enters a knowledge base.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Knowledge → Custom to review available pipeline templates.
Choose a template, name the base and create it. The base and pipeline are created together, then the canvas opens.
Review steps and configuration on the canvas before ingestion. Use a small document set to check the results.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Check document status and test retrieval after ingestion, rather than relying only on a saved pipeline.

pages.title: Connect external knowledge
pages.description: Connect an existing retrieval service in your organisation.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Connect an existing retrieval service in your organisation.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Settings → External knowledge and register a service name, endpoint and required key.
Create an external knowledge base and select the registered service and its external knowledge identifier.
Use Retrieval inside that base to send a test question and inspect the response. Attach the base to an application after a successful test.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: This service receives outbound queries; it differs from a source that imports documents. The destination must satisfy connection policies and data labels.

pages.title: Use extension APIs for moderation
pages.description: Register a moderation endpoint managed by your organisation.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Register a moderation endpoint managed by your organisation.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Integrations → Extension and enter a name, endpoint URL and an API key if required.
Use the test action to confirm the endpoint returns a valid moderation response.
In application configuration, open Moderation and select this endpoint instead of a moderation model. Test accepted and blocked inputs.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: An extension is an HTTP call to your endpoint, not a downloaded executable plugin. The endpoint receives user messages and follows outbound-access policy.

pages.title: Read logs and execution traces
pages.description: Trace application results back to conversations or execution steps.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Trace application results back to conversations or execution steps.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open an application and select Logs. The list shows conversations or workflow runs depending on application type.
Search within the loaded list, then open a conversation or execution trace.
Compare status, timestamps, token use and elapsed time. For workflows, inspect the failing step before changing the draft and retrying.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Distinguish per-application logs from aggregate Monitoring. Lists have loading limits, so searching does not necessarily cover all historical records.

pages.title: Set up canned answers
pages.description: Provide consistent answers to explicitly matched questions.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Provide consistent answers to explicitly matched questions.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Inside an application, open the logs and canned-answers area.
Add the question and approved answer using an account with annotation write permission.
Test an exact matching question and a similar question with different meaning before relying on the result.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: An exact match after normalisation returns the canned answer without a model call. Approximate matching is not used.

pages.title: Create roles and assign permissions
pages.description: Define workspace permissions around team responsibilities.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Define workspace permissions around team responsibilities.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Settings → Custom roles using an account allowed to manage roles.
Create a role, name it and select task-appropriate permissions. Granted permissions must stay within those you are allowed to grant.
Assign the role to members through workspace management and verify it with a member account before wider use.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Workspace roles do not automatically grant instance administration. Check both allowed operations and operations that must be denied.

pages.title: Manage S3 storage
pages.description: Monitor the bucket, storage use and unreferenced objects.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Monitor the bucket, storage use and unreferenced objects.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Settings → Storage to inspect bucket status, use, object counts and measurement time.
With quota-management permission, adjust limits as appropriate. Review object metadata to understand storage use.
Scan for unreferenced objects and review them before cleanup. When migrating from shared storage, move files first and clean the old bucket afterwards.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Usage reflects the latest measurement; exceeding the limit can block new uploads. Clean up only data confirmed as no longer needed.

pages.title: Configure single sign-on
pages.description: Connect an identity provider and map user groups.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.text: Connect an identity provider and map user groups.
sections.caption: AI Studio overview for this feature; illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Settings → Single sign-on. Add the issuer, client ID and credentials supplied by the identity administrator.
Select the default workspace, routing domain and optional group mapping. Use the exact claim name sent by the provider.
Test sign-in with a test account and verify workspace, role and clearance before enabling it for users.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: With group sync enabled, role and clearance refresh on each sign-in. Incorrect configuration can put users in the wrong workspace or leave them without needed access.

pages.title: Configure applications and multimodal features
pages.description: Configure inputs, conversation features, speech, image generation and business processes.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Configure inputs, conversation features, speech, image generation and business processes.
sections.caption: Related application interface with illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open draft configuration. Select the model, parameters and instructions; declare variables referenced by instruction or opening-message templates.
Open Features to configure the opening message, suggested questions and retrieval mode. Select speech recognition, text-to-speech or image-generation models when the relevant provider is configured.
For business-specific processes, define appropriate instructions and tools. Save the draft and test its inputs and each enabled feature before publishing.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: A configuration field does not mean its service is ready. Speech and image generation require supported models, permissions and a working connection.

pages.title: Evaluate and compare quality
pages.description: Use test datasets to track application quality across runs.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Use test datasets to track application quality across runs.
sections.caption: Related application interface with illustrative data.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Inside an application, open Monitoring and Evaluations. Create a dataset using the input format shown for that application type.
Enter questions and expected outputs. If generating test cases, choose topics, language and count, then review the generated dataset.
Run the evaluation, track status and inspect individual cases. Select compatible runs for comparison, and review failures before changing configuration.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.text: Evaluation results depend on the dataset and configuration. Training-data export under monitoring prepares data; it does not complete fine-tuning.

pages.title: Variables and input forms
pages.description: Collect structured data before an application runs.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Collect structured data before an application runs.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open the application → Configuration → Variables. Add a variable with an internal name and a user-facing label.
Choose the data type. For a select field, enter one option per line and use a default value of the correct type.
Set required status, length limits and sensitivity as appropriate. Order fields in the sequence users should complete them.
Reference variable names in the instruction or opening-message template. Save the draft and test valid, missing and incorrectly typed values in preview.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The form shows the correct labels, required fields are checked and values reach the intended instructions.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Cannot save: look for undeclared variables in templates. Invalid defaults: check numeric types, select options and variable names.

pages.title: Speech and image generation
pages.description: Enable speech input, spoken answers and image generation with supported models.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Enable speech input, spoken answers and image generation with supported models.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: In Model providers, configure speech recognition, TTS or text-to-image models for the required capability.
Open application → Configuration → Features. Select each specialised model rather than only a general LLM.
For TTS, enter a voice supported by the provider. For image generation, check that image_generate is available in the relevant tool configuration.
Save and test a short spoken input, a spoken response or an image request. Inspect the output before publishing.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The feature produces the expected output, rather than merely displaying a selected model.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Empty list: no usable model of that type is configured. Provider errors: check connectivity, voice name and browser microphone permission.

pages.title: Version history and restoration
pages.description: Restore earlier configuration into a draft while controlling publication.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Restore earlier configuration into a draft while controlling publication.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open version history in the application editor. Compare version numbers, models and Draft/Published badges.
Save or record unsaved changes before choosing Restore on the intended version.
Review the confirmation dialog and restore into the draft. Reopen configuration and compare important fields.
Run your test questions. Republish only after confirming the restored behaviour.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The draft contains the selected configuration; end users receive changes only after the appropriate publication step.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Restoration does not replace testing. Review unsaved-change warnings to avoid overwriting work.

pages.title: Run, trace and compare workflows
pages.description: Locate failing steps through each node’s actual inputs and outputs.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Locate failing steps through each node’s actual inputs and outputs.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open the Run panel, provide inputs matching the start node and run the draft.
Inspect Inputs, Result, Detail and Tracing. Select a node to inspect its process data and output.
Check waiting states: scheduled time, event, child workflow or approval. A waiting run is not necessarily a failure.
Open run history and compare two runs. Compare node status, elapsed time and labels before changing variable mappings.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The run reaches its expected output and differences between attempts can be traced to a node and its data.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Hidden node data: check clearance. Code-node failure: verify sandbox configuration; placing a node on the canvas does not make the runtime available.

pages.title: Import/export DSL and environment variables
pages.description: Move application structure between environments and configure secrets at the destination.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Move application structure between environments and configure secrets at the destination.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Export DSL from the workflow. Review application name, type and model/tool references in the file.
At the destination, choose Import app from DSL, paste content or choose a file, then confirm. Import creates a new application.
Open Environment variables in the new application. Supply required values again; DSL does not carry secret values.
Select models, knowledge bases and tools available at the destination, then test before publishing.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The new application has the correct structure, the original is unchanged and dependencies are configured.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Successful import followed by failure often means missing variables, models or tools. Saved secret values cannot be read back; an empty replacement field means unchanged.

pages.title: Reuse snippets and edit the canvas
pages.description: Save reusable structures and use the canvas editing tools.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Save reusable structures and use the canvas editing tools.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Snippets and save the current workflow with a task-oriented name. This saves the current whole graph.
Insert the snippet into the destination canvas. Inspect the new nodes and connect them to your flow.
Use the context menu, copy/paste and undo/redo to edit the structure. Add notes to explain important decisions.
Recheck variables and references after insertion, then test the added path.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Inserted nodes have their own IDs and do not collide with existing canvas IDs.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: A snippet does not configure destination connections or secrets. Reconnect disconnected ports and inspect inputs before running.

pages.title: Webhooks, schedules and event retries
pages.description: Attach triggers to workflows and track incoming events.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Attach triggers to workflows and track incoming events.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Save the workflow first, select a webhook or schedule trigger node and open its binding configuration.
For schedules, enter cron and check the displayed timezone. For webhooks, save the signing secret when first shown.
Map payload fields into input variables. Choose JSON or FHIR Bundle for the corresponding source, and set an hourly cap.
Send a test event, filter Received events by status and open the linked run. Retry failed events only after checking their cause.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The event appears, links to a run and completes or waits as designed.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: No run: check enabled state, signature, cron and mappings. Disabling preserves the current secret; rotating it requires sender updates.

pages.title: Configure API tools
pages.description: Let agents call APIs registered in the workspace.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Let agents call APIs registered in the workspace.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Integrations → Tools → API and inspect existing definitions.
Add or edit a definition using the form; match its operation schema, inputs and authentication to the service documentation.
Check the destination against egress policy. Attach the tool to an application and select the required operations.
Run a sample task through the agent and inspect the tool call, parameters and result in logs.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The agent calls the intended API and uses its returned data in the test task.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Authentication failure: check credentials. Missing tool: check workspace configuration and application tool selection.

pages.title: Connect MCP servers
pages.description: Discover and select MCP operations for agents.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Discover and select MCP operations for agents.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Integrations → Tools → MCP and add the server address and authentication required by the form.
Check connectivity and inspect the operations exposed by the server. Review the input schema of the needed operation.
In the agent application, attach the MCP connection and choose operations relevant to its task.
Run a test task and inspect the actual call in logs, including a server-error case.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Operations are discovered, selectable and invoked with the expected inputs.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Discovery failure: check URL, authentication and egress. A working connection does not mean it has been attached to an application.

pages.title: Use workflows as tools
pages.description: Reuse a workflow through a tool interface.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Reuse a workflow through a tool interface.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Prepare a workflow with clear inputs and mapped end-node outputs, and test it first.
Open Integrations → Tools → Workflow to inspect available workflows and configure the provided tool interface.
Attach the tool to an agent or another workflow’s tool node and map input parameters.
Run the caller and inspect traces for both the caller and the invoked workflow.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The caller receives the workflow’s expected output and waiting/error states are traceable.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Missing output: inspect the end node. Missing workflow: check permissions, application type and required publication state.

pages.title: Manage outbound connections
pages.description: Configure allowed destinations for tools and external services.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Configure allowed destinations for tools and external services.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Integrations → Tools → Egress using an account allowed to manage connections.
Compare the service hostname and port with the allowlist and add the required destination.
Review data labels, provider type and network-zone configuration before running the application.
Test an allowed call and one that should be denied using sample data, then inspect errors and logs.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Policy-compliant calls pass and disallowed calls are explicitly rejected.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Adding a URL does not change data labels. When blocked, inspect labels, destinations and permissions together rather than opening the whole network.

pages.title: Folders, filtering and moving documents
pages.description: Organise knowledge documents and act on the intended scope.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Organise knowledge documents and act on the intended scope.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open a knowledge base → Documents. Search by name and filter processing status when needed.
Create or select a folder in the navigation tree. Check its path before adding documents.
Select documents to move and choose the destination folder. For bulk operations, review the selected count.
Open the destination, locate the document and check status; a filtered-out document has not necessarily been deleted.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Documents appear in the intended folder and filters do not lead to unintended selections.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Missing document: clear filters and check the current folder. Moving a folder does not change content or security labels.

pages.title: Inspect and edit knowledge chunks
pages.description: Edit the content actually used for retrieval.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Edit the content actually used for retrieval.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open a processed document and inspect its extracted chunks alongside the original.
Edit content or keywords in the relevant chunk, or add a chunk for missing information.
Enable or disable chunks to control their use. Check the visible selection scope before bulk operations.
Save and test a related retrieval query, checking that disabled chunks are not selected.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The edited chunk appears in retrieval results as intended.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Stale result: check saving, indexing status and the tested base. For PDF/OCR, compare extracted text with the original page.

pages.title: Review memories and their evidence
pages.description: Decide what may be reused in later AI turns.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Decide what may be reused in later AI turns.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Memory → Awaiting review with memory-administration permission. Inspect each proposal’s owner, application and label.
Read the draft-versus-edit comparison. If evidence is unavailable, review the warning before deciding.
Approve appropriate information or reject incorrect information. Approved memories may enter that subject’s later prompts.
Open Store and Activity to verify the resulting state and the recorded action.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The proposal changes state correctly and memories are not confused between subjects.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: No approval rate may simply mean no decisions exist yet. A missing diff calls for review, not automatic approval.

pages.title: Configure, retain and disable memory
pages.description: Control extraction frequency, retention and data when disabling memory.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Control extraction frequency, retention and data when disabling memory.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Memory → Settings. Inspect the extraction model and current limits.
Adjust message-based extraction frequency, retention and limits for your needs, then save.
Before enabling memories for public-link visitors, review the cookie-based identity behaviour.
When disabling, choose to keep data unused or follow the deletion process. Purging requires a separate action and confirmation after extraction is off.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Settings persist after reload and disabling does not silently delete data beyond confirmed actions.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Saving settings does not mean data has been purged. Changing a visitor cookie changes the memory identity.

pages.title: Export training data
pages.description: Prepare application data before submitting a training job.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Prepare application data before submitting a training job.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open application → Monitoring → Training data export with the required permission.
Review the data scope and notice before exporting, confirming suitability for training.
Choose download or the configured object store. Wait for the result and inspect exported and label-excluded counts.
Review the data and remove inappropriate material before using it in model training.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: A file or stored export exists with record counts; fine-tuning remains a separate step.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Fewer records than expected: inspect label exclusions and permissions rather than relaxing policy to increase the count.

pages.title: Invite members and control access
pages.description: Place people in the correct workspace, role and departments.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Place people in the correct workspace, role and departments.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Settings → Workspace → Members and choose Invite member.
Enter the email, select a role and assign permitted department and clearance limits.
The recipient opens the invitation and completes acceptance/sign-in. Check membership status afterwards.
When changing roles or removing members, check the selected workspace and review the effect before saving.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Members enter the correct workspace and see actions appropriate to their permissions.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Missing invitation control: check member-management permission. SSO group sync may refresh roles at the next sign-in.

pages.title: Token and request quotas
pages.description: Set usage limits for the appropriate scope and period.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Set usage limits for the appropriate scope and period.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open Quotas in workspace management. Choose an available organisation, workspace, application or provider scope.
Select the daily/monthly period and token/request ceilings. Check the meaning of empty values and zero before saving.
Monitor usage and ceiling-reached state, comparing them with Monitoring statistics.
Start a new period or delete a quota only after reviewing its effect on further usage.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The quota applies to the intended subject and period, with visible usage.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Blocked below an application’s own limit: check higher-level quotas. No limit and a zero limit are different states.

pages.title: Workspace API keys and MCP capabilities
pages.description: Issue scoped keys for integrating systems.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Issue scoped keys for integrating systems.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Open workspace management → API keys, create a key and give it a recognisable name.
Choose application scope and expiry. The default runs applications only; select mcp:author or mcp:admin only when needed.
Save the key when first shown in your secret-management system, then test the integration with its granted scope.
For workspace administration over MCP, use an app-unscoped key with mcp:admin and enable the MCP admin gate. Revoke unused keys.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: The key calls granted capabilities and stops working after expiry or revocation.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: Declaring mcp:admin is insufficient while the admin gate is off. Some permissions, including others’ memories and provider credentials, never transfer over MCP.

pages.title: Organisations and instance quotas
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Inspect organisations, status, workspace counts and membership.
Review the MFA floor and organisation quotas. Use the relevant workspace settings or operational procedure for changes; this overview is read-only.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Organisations and workspaces are different scopes; verify the intended target.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Instance accounts
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Locate an account using displayed information and inspect its current state.
Make a permitted change, review the confirmation and reload the list.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Managing an instance account differs from removing one workspace membership.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Check service health
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Open Health and inspect dependency and migration states.
Correlate errors with the affected service, follow its operational procedure and refresh.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Health status does not replace an application run; also test a user task.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Change runtime settings
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Open Runtime settings, locate the key and inspect its value source.
Edit a permitted setting, save and allow the refresh interval shown on the page.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Secret settings expose configured state rather than a read-back of the secret.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Network zones and destinations
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Open Network and inspect the effective network zone and allowed destinations.
This page reports effective network-zone and allowlist configuration. Change the underlying deployment settings or allowlist files through operations procedures, then refresh.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Network configuration, data labels and destination rules jointly affect calls.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Control feature flags
pages.description: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.

sections.title: Where to work
sections.text: Operations for AI Studio instance administrators.
sections.caption: Related workspace overview. Follow the navigation steps below to open this feature.

sections.title: Step-by-step
steps: Sign in as an instance administrator and open the corresponding Administration page. Workspace ownership alone does not grant this access.
Open Feature flags and read descriptions and current state before making changes.
This page is read-only. Change feature-flag configuration through the deployment process, then refresh this page and test the affected flow.
Reload to verify effective state and review the effect on applications in use.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Enabling a flag does not install missing providers or infrastructure.

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.text: If access is denied, check instance-administration access. Change read-only settings through deployment procedures rather than trying to edit them here.

pages.title: Design agent business processes
pages.description: Separate goals and instructions into processes selected for each user request.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Separate goals and instructions into processes selected for each user request.
sections.caption: Related editor or deployment overview; use the steps below to open the relevant settings.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open Configuration → Features → Business processes. Add a name and a description of when to use it.
Provide the goal, instructions, constraints and example questions. Make descriptions distinct to reduce incorrect routing.
Choose Reason & Act, Fixed plan or Run a tool. Run a tool requires exactly one tool; other modes can restrict the allowed tool set.
Save and test representative questions for each process plus ambiguous cases. Inspect results and refine descriptions when routing is wrong.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Each turn carries one selected process’s instructions. With no processes, the application follows the system prompt.

sections.title: Checks and limitations
sections.text: No available tools: attach tools to the application first. With two or more processes, routing can add a model call.

pages.title: Web apps, embedding and chat experience
pages.description: Deliver a published application through a link or embedded widget.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Deliver a published application through a link or embedded widget.
sections.caption: Related editor or deployment overview; use the steps below to open the relevant settings.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Publish a tested draft, then open Deploy → Web sharing. Read any blocking reason before enabling it.
Enable sharing and use the provided link or embed code. Test in a separate browser session as a visitor.
In Features, configure the opening message, suggested and follow-up questions, charts and visitor attachments as appropriate.
Test conversations and sample attachments; check image-model capability, quotas and responses. After disabling sharing, retest the old link.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Visitors access the intended published version; disabling sharing stops the link from serving the application as before.

sections.title: Checks and limitations
sections.text: Public attachments consume workspace storage; follow-up questions can add model calls. Console attachment support differs from visitor permissions.

pages.title: Connect messaging channels
pages.description: Connect a published application to a supported communication channel.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Connect a published application to a supported communication channel.
sections.caption: Related editor or deployment overview; use the steps below to open the relevant settings.

sections.title: Steps
steps: Open application → Deploy and inspect the channel gallery. Choose the platform used by your team.
Open channel configuration and provide credentials, identifiers and callback details required by the form.
Complete the corresponding platform setup and enable the connection. Ensure the application has a published version.
Send a test message from the actual channel and inspect the reply and logs. Retest after changing credentials or the published version.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.text: Messages traverse the channel and receive replies from the correct application, beyond merely saving configuration.

sections.title: Checks and limitations
sections.text: Receiving without replying: check publication, callbacks, credentials and bot permissions. Channel availability depends on deployment and platform configuration.

pages.title: Workflow node reference
pages.description: Choose and configure the 28 node types available in the editor.

sections.title: Choose a node for the task
sections.text: The current editor exposes 28 node types. Add a node, configure its fields, connect its ports and test its inputs/outputs before publishing.
sections.caption: Workflow editor overview with an illustrative three-node flow.

sections.title: Start points, AI and data
sections.text: Declare inputs at the start or trigger node. Select models/instructions for LLM and agent nodes, and a base/query for retrieval. Map the answer or output fields at the end.
steps: Start
LLM
Knowledge retrieval

End
Agent

sections.title: Understand requests
sections.text: Define clear classes and connect each classifier branch. For parameter extraction, define names, types and expected information; test missing-data cases.
steps: Question classifier
Parameter extractor

sections.title: Conditions and loops
sections.text: Cover conditional branches and defaults. A decision table returns values; add If/Else to branch on them. For iteration/loops, define inputs and termination conditions.
steps: If / Else
Decision table

Loop

sections.title: Transform data
sections.text: Select the correct inputs, types and outputs. Test templates, variable aggregation/assignment, lists and document extraction on small data. Code nodes require an operations-configured sandbox.
steps: Template
Variable aggregator
Variable assigner
List operator
Document extractor
Code

sections.title: Integrations and outputs
sections.text: Configure permitted HTTP destinations, tools or channels. For knowledge writes, select the destination base and inspect ingestion status. Check authentication, schemas and egress policy.
steps: HTTP request
Tool
Send via channel
Write to knowledge

sections.title: Waits and approvals
sections.text: Configure resume time/events and required reviewer input. When a run stops here, inspect its waiting state and approval queue before treating it as a failure.

Human input

landing.image_note: AI Studio interface with example data.

panels.label: Applications
panels.title: Start with a useful assistant.
panels.text: Choose an application type, write instructions, and test answers in the preview panel. Refine your draft before publishing.

panels.label: Knowledge
panels.title: Give your documents context.
panels.text: Create a knowledge base, add documents, and connect it to your application so AI has the right information for the task.

panels.label: Workflows
panels.title: Design every step AI takes.
panels.text: Connect inputs, models, and outputs on a visual canvas. Extend the workflow to match your team’s needs.

panels.label: Tools
panels.title: Connect AI to the tools you use.
panels.text: Explore tools and MCP connections configured in your workspace. Choose the operations that fit your application’s task.
